newsitem.title: UK: BoE welcomes EMI report on monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: BoE welcomes EMI report on monetary policy.

text.p: The Bank of England said on Friday it welcomed a report from the European Monetary Institute on the operational framework for monetary policy in stage three of EMU.
"We welcome the substance of the report which in our view provides a practical framework for the European Central Bank's future monetary policy operations," the Bank said in a statement.
The Bank said it welcomed the report's conclusions on monetary strategy, namely to achieve price stability by either monetary targets or inflation targets.

"The Bank also welcomes the main elements of the framework to implement the strategy," it said. The EMI said these would comprise a corridor within which overnight market interest rates would be expected to lie.
The Bank said it endorsed the EMI's proposal that both public and high-quality private sector paper should be eligible for use by counterparties in monetary operations.

"If the UK were to join stage three, we expect that the full range of instruments available for monetary operations under the Bank's reform proposals announced last Deceber would continue to be useable," it said.
The Bank reiterated its opposition to the possible use of reserve requirements under stage three.
"The Bank has consistently argued against their actual use, and would continue to do so, in the ECB, if the UK were to join the Monetary Union," it said.

The Bank did not comment on the unresolved debate about access by non-euro area countries to intraday liquidity on the same terms as euro are countries under TARGET, merely noting it had published its views on this last month.
